01 / THE QUESTION

What needed to work?

Different syntax can obscure the shared ideas behind parsing, type checking, optimization, and execution.

An educational compiler and browser IDE exposing tokens, syntax recognition, AST, types, typed IR, bytecode and VM execution.

03 / THE ENGINEERING

The decision behind it.

Use six restricted syntax families with one semantic model. Run the same Python compiler in a browser worker through Pyodide instead of inventing a second compiler.

  1. 01Lexer & parser
  2. 02AST & semantic analysis
  3. 03Typed IR & optimization
  4. 04Bytecode & stack VM
  • Built a lexer, parser, AST, semantic analysis, typed intermediate representation, bytecode format, and stack virtual machine.
  • Implemented arrays, recursion, scope and type checks, and bounded execution.
  • Added constant folding, branch simplification, and dead-code elimination.
  • Created a shared CLI and browser IDE with compiler-stage inspection and reusable bytecode artifacts. Browser execution runs through Pyodide in a Web Worker.
PythonJavaScriptTyped IRCustom bytecode VMPyodide / WebAssembly

04 / THE EVIDENCE

What the work demonstrates.

The mixed-language program produces 0, 1, 3, 6, 12, then “done.” These are actual saved compiler records; the included IDE lets you run your own program.

The preview is backed by saved runs from the actual compiler. The complete IDE runs the same Python implementation through a browser worker.

05 / THE BOUNDARIES

What I can stand behind.

A restricted educational language, not an implementation of six complete languages. Browser execution remains bounded.

Building something useful means being precise about what it does, what has been checked, and what still needs to be tested.
